0.0.n: おなか is an everyday, gentle word for the belly.

0.1.n: が marks おなか as what becomes empty in this expression.

0.2.n: Polite past form of すく; おなかがすく is the usual expression for getting hungry.

1.0.n: The internal の links 山 to 上, specifying which place is meant.

1.1.n: の links the location 山の上 to レストラン, telling us where the restaurant is.

1.2.n: This word borrowed from English is written in katakana.

1.3.n: に marks the restaurant as the destination of the movement.

1.4.n: Polite form of 行く; here it describes a planned action.

2.0.n: ちょっと softens the description of how difficult the climb is.

2.1.n: たいへん describes something demanding or difficult, here the climb.

2.2.n: です makes the description polite.

2.3.n: が connects two contrasting thoughts: the climb is difficult, yet the speaker will do it.

2.5.n: 山の上 names the high location the speaker is heading toward.

2.6.n: に marks 山の上 as the destination of the climb.

2.7.n: Polite form of のぼる; here it expresses the speaker's intended upward movement.

3.0.n: 分 counts minutes; １０分 is read じゅっぷん or じっぷん.

3.1.n: くらい follows a quantity to show that it is approximate.

3.2.n: て-form of あるく, linking the walking to the arrival that follows.

3.4.n: Here it refers back to the restaurant the speaker planned to visit.

3.5.n: に marks the place reached when used with つく.

3.6.n: Polite past form of つく, showing that the speaker has reached the destination.

4.0.n: とても strengthens the description きれい.

4.1.n: きれい can also mean clean, but here it describes the scenery's beauty.

4.2.n: な connects きれい to the noun けしき that it describes.

4.3.n: けしき refers to the landscape or view visible from a place.

4.4.n: です politely completes the statement about the view.

0.tip: おなかがすく literally describes an empty stomach but naturally means to get hungry.

1.lit: [I] will go to the restaurant at the top of the mountain.
1.tip: 山の上の modifies レストラン: the location comes before the noun it describes.

2.lit: [It] is a little tough, but [I] will climb to the top of the mountain.
2.tip: です links with が to politely say something is true, but introduce a contrasting thought.

3.lit: [I] walked about ten minutes and arrived at the restaurant.
3.tip: The て-form links the actions in order, while the final verb shows that they happened in the past.

4.tip: きれい needs な before a noun, even though it ends in い.
